A bounded follow-up applies the pinned selected bit histogram to that changed law to measure how far the actual profile remains from the aggregate floor before pursuing any new endpoint.
bottleneck_link: A fixed rank-mass budget and child-rank cap impose a lower bound on the recursive moment. This proves whether either supplier can reach a=1/9 even after granting perfect high-rank repacking and deleting centre cost.
stop_rule: Stop this aggregate screen once the strict a=1/9 obstruction and exact unpaid/rank boundaries are certified. Do not expand to another search unless one complete dirty endpoint or row-coefficient invoice can realize a passing boundary with margin.
evidence: Exact rational ninth-power comparisons prove that with one unpaid coordinate the centre-free minimum moment is >1 at bit R=53 and complex R=51. At the current caps, the ideal aggregate floor first drops below one at bit u=2 and complex u=3 centre-free / u=4 with centre retained. The pinned paired-plane identity-fit candidate (u=2,c=112) has floor approximately 1.02818 at a=1/9 and also needs u=4 to pass this aggregate budget. With one unpaid coordinate, deleting centre requires R=56 (bit) and R=65 (complex), first allowed by the halving guard at depths 6 and 6. This is a necessary-budget screen only; no supplier, replacement coverage identity, or higher-depth row invoice is constructed. For the pinned selected bit histogram, u=2 and R=53 still give moment 1.365696 with the centre and 1.355508 without it. If all 5,129 local rank mass is fractionally repacked at a uniform rank, first passing ranks are 53 with the centre (rank52 gives 1.001209) and 48 centre-free (rank47 gives 1.000411). This is a fixed-profile screen only.
